findings.reason: a node cannot satisfy both arms of clause (1) and, with `matches quantity by quantity` carrying no tolerance, will either weaken the gate or compare the wrong product.
findings.text: §2 done-when (1) states that the translated CORSICA 130506/6 DD3 read "also matches the repository's DD 4.1.0 conversion of the same case (`iter_corsica_130506` in `tests/data-manifest.json`), which passes through bit-identically as the DD4 fixture", but that manifest entry is not a conversion of the pulse: it is an `efitpp_validator_layers` case with two differently-roled layers (`iter_corsica_130506_input.nc`, 4398124 B, role `input`; `iter_corsica_130506.nc`, 827510 B, role `reference`) and `reference_slices: 4`, against the census's DD 3.41.0 imasdb run `/work/imas/shared/imasdb/ITER/3/130506/6` with 55 of 56 slices above 1 MA; no DD4 130506 exists in the imasdb (`ls /work/imas/shared/imasdb/ITER/4/130506/` is absent), so the bit-identity is asserted between a full-pulse read and a 4-slice validator case whose reference layer is itself a held solution

findings.reason: deleting the shim is the same action whether or not importers exist, and done-when (3)'s search reports the zero either way.
findings.text: §2 says of the shim, "its importers name `nova_cocos` directly", but `nova/io/cocos.py` has no importer anywhere under `nova/`, `scripts/`, `tests/` or `packages/` (a search for `nova.io.cocos` and `from nova.io import cocos` returns only the module's own docstring), so the migration this sentence describes has no target
